summary: 36 items, but the mix is skewed toward cocktail/bar spirits and niche detail (4 cachaça variants, 6 bitters entries, absinthe/aquavit/ouzo/grappa/schnapps) while almost every workhorse COOKING alcohol is missing. There is no dry white wine, red wine, Marsala, sherry, port, Madeira, vermouth, Shaoxing rice wine, mirin, cognac, salted 'cooking wine', or any concrete liqueur (Grand Marnier/triple sec, amaretto, Kahlua) — the recipe-critical core. Existing parents (wine, fortified-wine, rice-wine, liqueur, whiskey, cachaça, bitters) are good hooks for expansion. Several well-formedness problems exist: bourbon over-claims the generic 'whiskey/whisky' aliases (collides with the whiskey parent), shochu's aliases wrongly include 'korean soju' (a separate item), schnapps-herbal/aquavit-herbal/sake inherit copy-pasted aliases from their parent, and wine/fortified-wine aliases bleed into each other ('vin'/'vino'/'wines' on both). Storage/freshness is reasonable for unopened spirits but the wine and rice-wine families need an after-opening Refrigerated track. Mirin and (often) Shaoxing 'cooking wine' straddle the Alcohol vs Condiments line — flagged below.
issues: Comprehensiveness: missing the most-used cooking alcohols entirely — dry white wine, red wine, Marsala, sherry (dry/cream), port, Madeira, dry vermouth, sweet (red) vermouth, Shaoxing rice wine, mirin, sake-for-cooking, cognac, and salted 'cooking wine'. These appear in far more recipes than absinthe/aquavit/ouzo/cachaça variants.

Comprehensiveness: no concrete liqueurs despite the parent 'liqueur' existing. Recipes call for orange liqueur (triple sec / Grand Marnier / Cointreau-style), amaretto, coffee liqueur (Kahlua-style), Irish cream, and creme de cassis by name.
Comprehensiveness: only generic 'beer'. Cooking distinguishes lager, ale, stout (braises, batters, chili) — at minimum 'stout' and 'ale' as children of beer would help recipe matching.
Comprehensiveness: 'whiskey' has no scotch/Scotch whisky or Irish whiskey and only 'bourbon' as a concrete child; rye whiskey is also common.

Well-formedness: bourbon.aliases = ['bourbons','whiskeys','whiskies','whisky'] — bourbon (a child) should NOT claim the generic whiskey/whisky/whiskies aliases; that text belongs to the 'whiskey' parent and will cause a generic 'whisky' input to resolve to bourbon.
Well-formedness: shochu.aliases includes 'korean soju' even though 'soju' is its own catalog item; shochu (Japanese) and soju (Korean) are distinct and should not cross-alias.

Well-formedness: rice-wine and sake both list alias 'rice wines'; sake is a child of rice-wine yet duplicates the parent's plural alias. sake also missing 'sake wine' / common romanizations are fine but the inherited 'rice wines' should be dropped on the child.

Well-formedness: aquavit-herbal and schnapps-herbal copy their parent's aliases verbatim ('akvavit','aqua vitae','aquavits' / 'german schnapps','schnaaps','schnappses','schnaps'), so a generic 'aquavit'/'schnapps' input can mis-route to the herbal child.
Parent-child: 'fortified wine' exists as a child of 'wine' but has NO concrete children (Marsala, sherry, port, Madeira, vermouth) — the whole fortified family is empty.
Parent-child: 'rice wine' parent has only 'sake' under it; the two other major cooking rice wines (Shaoxing, mirin) are absent.
Parent-child: 'liqueur' and 'fruit-liqueur'/'liqueur-herbal' exist but no named liqueurs hang off them.

Storage/freshness: 'wine' has Refrigerated [3,7] (good for after opening) but 'fortified-wine' Refrigerated [30,60] is generous vs real-world (sherry ~1 month, vermouth ~2 months, Marsala ~1-6 months) — acceptable as a cooking-tolerant range. New fortified children should mirror the parent's Refrigerated track.

Storage/freshness: 'rice-wine'/'sake' Refrigerated [30,90] is reasonable; Shaoxing should match (~6-12mo unopened pantry, refrigerate after opening). Salted cooking versions last much longer and warrant a separate item.

Categorisation: mirin is a sweetened rice 'wine' but is functionally a seasoning/condiment; many catalogs file it under Condiments/Sauces. Recommend adding it here (it is alcoholic and a rice-wine sibling) but note the overlap. Likewise 'Shaoxing cooking wine' (the salted supermarket version) is sold as a condiment in many regions.

Categorisation: 'cooking wine' (salted) is technically a seasoning and is often shelf-stable for ~1 year after opening — distinct enough from drinking wine to be its own item; flagged so it is not conflated with 'wine'.
redundancies: Both list alias 'agave spirit'. Tequila is a legally-defined subset of agave spirits and mezcal is the broader category — the shared generic alias 'agave spirit' will make 'agave spirit' inputs ambiguous. Keep 'agave spirit' on mezcal (broader) and remove it from tequila, or add a generic 'agave-spirit' parent.

bourbon.aliases duplicate the parent whiskey's generic aliases ('whiskeys','whiskies','whisky'); a bare 'whisky'/'whiskey' input would match both. The generic terms should live only on the 'whiskey' parent.
shochu.aliases includes 'korean soju' while 'soju' is a separate item — overlapping alias between two distinct entries.
Both carry alias 'rice wines'; the child duplicating the parent's generic plural is redundant and dilutes parent matching.
Identical alias set copied to the herbal child ('akvavit','aqua vitae','aquavits').
Identical alias set copied to the herbal child ('german schnapps','schnaaps','schnappses','schnaps').

newItems.name: dry white wine
newItems.notes: By far the most common cooking wine — pan sauces, risotto, mussels, deglazing. Refrigerate after opening; ~3-5 days for drinking quality, longer is fine for cooking. Vegan only if not fined with isinglass/gelatin, but tag Vegan to match the existing 'wine' parent default.

newItems.name: red wine
newItems.notes: Braises (coq au vin, beef bourguignon, ragu), reductions. Mirrors 'wine' storage. Vegan caveat same as white wine.

newItems.name: cooking wine
newItems.notes: Salt-added supermarket 'cooking wine' — shelf-stable ~1 year+ after opening because of added salt/preservatives; distinct from drinking wine. Functionally a seasoning; flagged in issues as straddling Alcohol vs Condiments.

newItems.name: marsala wine
newItems.notes: Chicken/veal Marsala, mushroom sauces, tiramisu. Fortified — refrigerate after opening; keeps weeks (sweet) to months (dry); cooking-grade with salt lasts ~1 year.

newItems.name: sherry
newItems.notes: Dry sherry for Chinese stir-fries (Shaoxing substitute), bisques, sauces; cream sherry for desserts. Fortified — refrigerate opened, ~1 month drinking quality.

newItems.name: port wine
newItems.notes: Pan sauces, reductions, fruit/cheese desserts. Sweet fortified — keeps longer than table wine once opened (refrigerated up to ~1 year).

newItems.name: madeira wine
newItems.notes: Sauces (Madeira sauce), reductions, gravies. Already-oxidised/heated in production, so it is extremely robust once opened — months at room temp.

newItems.name: dry vermouth
newItems.notes: Common white-wine substitute in pan sauces, chicken/fish, risotto. Aromatized fortified wine — best refrigerated after opening (~2 months); flavor flattens fast at room temp (~1 month).

newItems.name: sweet vermouth
newItems.notes: Braises and Italian sauces; refrigerate after opening like dry vermouth.

newItems.name: shaoxing wine
newItems.notes: The essential Chinese cooking rice wine — stir-fries, marinades, braises, dumpling fillings. Refrigerate after opening (~6-12 months). Salted supermarket version sold as a condiment in some regions (noted in issues).

newItems.name: mirin
newItems.notes: Sweet Japanese rice wine for teriyaki, glazes, simmered dishes, sushi rice. ~3-6 months after opening. Straddles Alcohol vs Condiments — many catalogs file it under Condiments/Sauces; placed here as a rice-wine sibling with that overlap flagged. Hon-mirin best at cool room temp (sugars crystallize cold); aji-mirin seasoning fine refrigerated.

newItems.name: cognac
newItems.notes: Flambe, lobster bisque, pan sauces, pate. Subset of brandy; very long shelf life like other spirits.

newItems.name: calvados
newItems.notes: Apple brandy for pork, chicken, apple desserts (French cooking). Subset of brandy.

newItems.name: scotch whisky
newItems.notes: Sauces, marinades, whisky cream sauces. Concrete child to balance bourbon under 'whiskey'.

newItems.name: irish whiskey
newItems.notes: Irish coffee, cream sauces, baking. Concrete whiskey child.

newItems.name: stout
newItems.notes: Beef-and-stout braises, stews, chocolate stout cake, batters. Mirrors 'beer' storage. NOT Gluten-Free (barley) — note the dietaryTags difference from spirits.

newItems.name: ale
newItems.notes: Beer-batter, chili, braises. NOT Gluten-Free (barley/wheat).

newItems.name: orange liqueur
newItems.notes: Crepes Suzette, flambe, cranberry sauce, desserts, marinades. Generic name with the common brand/style terms as aliases (per 'keep generic' guidance). Child of fruit-liqueur.

newItems.name: coffee liqueur
newItems.notes: Tiramisu, espresso martinis, desserts, cakes. Sugar-heavy; long shelf life but quality fades after a few years. Kept Dairy-Free/Vegan (most coffee liqueurs are dairy-free; cream versions differ).

newItems.name: amaretto
newItems.notes: Almond-flavored liqueur for desserts, tiramisu, baking. NOT Nut-Free by name/flavor association (typically apricot-kernel based, but the almond branding means it should not carry a Nut-Free tag in a kitchen-safety context).

newItems.name: irish cream liqueur
newItems.notes: Desserts, coffee, cheesecakes, no-churn ice cream. Contains dairy cream — best refrigerated after opening; NOT Vegan/Dairy-Free (differs from every other spirit in this category).

cleanups.fix: Remove generic whiskey aliases ['whiskeys','whiskies','whisky'] from bourbon; keep only bourbon-specific terms (e.g. 'bourbons', 'bourbon whiskey'). The generic whiskey/whisky terms belong on the 'whiskey' parent.
Remove 'korean soju' from shochu.aliases — soju is a separate catalog item. Keep 'japanese shochu','shochus'.
Drop the redundant 'korean soju' duplication concern by ensuring it is the sole owner of soju terms; consider adding 'soju' and 'korean rice spirit' but it should not share aliases with shochu.
Remove 'rice wines' alias (it is the parent rice-wine's plural); keep 'japanese rice wine','nihonshu','sakes'. Optionally add 'cooking sake'.
Remove the copied parent aliases ['akvavit','aqua vitae','aquavits'] so generic aquavit input routes to the 'aquavit' parent, not the herbal child.
Remove the copied parent aliases ['german schnapps','schnaaps','schnappses','schnaps'] so generic schnapps input routes to the 'schnapps' parent.
Remove generic 'agave spirit' alias (it overlaps with mezcal, the broader agave category); keep 'tequilas'. Optionally keep 'agave spirit' only on mezcal.

Now that concrete fortified children (marsala/sherry/port/madeira/vermouth) are proposed, trim the bleed-over generic wine aliases ('vin','vino','wines') so they stay on the 'wine' parent and do not double-match here.
